description.narrative: Over 90% of the labour force in micro and small enterprises and more than half of the global labour force is employed in the informal sector which is commonly characterised with limited workplace rights and facilities (UNHCR, 2018). The informal economy in Liberia is estimated at 42.7% which is approximately USD 6 billion at GDP PPP levels (Worldeconomics.com, World Bank 2023a) A huge percentage of the Liberian youth estimated at 80% acquire their skills in the informal sector (TVET Policy, 2022-2027). About 70 % of the training providers offer informal or non-formal on-the-job based skills delivery. At the same time, Liberia’s unemployment rate is at 3.63 % (World Bank) and more than 50% of Liberians live below Poverty line (USAID Liberia, October 2022). Cumulatively, Liberia faces significant challenges in its education sector, including many out-of-school children, over-age enrolments, and inadequate access to education. Most Women and youth are therefore engaged in the informal sector , possessing valuable skills and competencies that remain unrecognized due to systematic challenges such as the absence of a functional recognition and certification system. Therefore, RPL (Recognition of Prior Learning) remains a potential solution to address the higher rate of unrecognized skills among the youth and women and create opportunities for these individuals to access decent jobs and contribute to the country's socioeconomic progress. RPL presents a win-win situation for all; adults seeking RPL, providers offering RPL, employers requiring certified human resources, unions aligned with each stakeholder interest and the state which is responsible for the citizens welfare as well as the economy. RPL is a quick solution to promote employability, enhance inclusion and increase productivity
